research_scope: Five complete source-free module-theoretic formulation reviews; no source research, new definitions or automatic alias.

amendments.review_rationale: Full-formulation review of Mittag-Leffler tensor-product comparison, flatness and faithful flatness, transfinite direct-sum dévissage, and finite module presentation; preserved all source versions and previous references without conflating defining exactness predicates and reusable constructions.
amendments.reason: Source-free Wave2 Pass2 contextual consolidation of module products, exactness, module filtrations and finite presentations; provisional candidate audit remains outstanding.

references.context: Module theory: categorical direct product ∏_{i∈I}Q_i of a possibly infinite indexed family of R-modules, consisting of all tuples with coordinatewise addition and scalar multiplication.
references.reason: A product of modules is independently meaningful and differs from the finite-support direct sum.
references.matching_note: Use arbitrary products, not the coproduct/direct-sum module construction.

references.context: Module theory: canonical R-linear map M⊗_R(∏_iQ_i)→∏_i(M⊗_R Q_i) induced by projection π_i:∏_iQ_i→Q_i; injectivity for all families defines Mittag-Leffler property.
references.reason: The canonical natural transformation between tensor of products and product of tensors is reusable even when it is not injective.
references.matching_note: No claim the comparison is always surjective; tensor products and module products differ.

references.disposition: Every indexed family is permitted; the map need not be surjective and the index set need not be countable.

references.context: Module theory: additive covariant tensor functor T_M:N↦N⊗_R M on R-modules, sending morphism f to f⊗id_M (for commutative R); not merely an individual tensor-product module.
references.reason: The flatness criterion concerns functorial action on sequences of morphisms.
references.matching_note: Preserve commutative-ring/bimodule tensor-sided conventions; avoid small-category restrictions.

references.phrase: preservation of exactness by tensor functor
references.disposition: Exactness preservation of every R-module sequence is precisely the defining criterion of flatness in this formulation, not a prerequisite concept of flatness itself.

references.phrase: flatness does not assert reflection of exactness
references.disposition: Faithful flatness is the strictly stronger criterion; this formulation requires preservation only.

references.context: Module theory: additive tensor functor T_M:N↦N⊗_R M on R-modules, with induced f⊗id_M on maps; the same operation used in the flat-module formulation.
references.reason: The functor is independently reusable even when reflection of exactness fails.
references.matching_note: Compare to flat-module tensor functor in global candidate consolidation.

references.disposition: The requirement that every sequence whose tensor image is exact must itself be exact is the *defining additional predicate* of faithful flatness. Preserve the distinction from simple preservation, which is flatness.
Faithful flatness requires both directions for arbitrary module sequences; applying M to a single exact sequence is not sufficient.

references.matching_note: The ambient M is an ordinary unital module over R.
The filtration is indexed by ordinals.
Each member of the increasing chain is a submodule of M.
Continuity of the filtration is imposed at limit ordinal stages.

references.phrase: successor inclusion splits as a direct summand
references.context: Module theory: split inclusion M_α↪M_{α+1} in an ordinal-indexed module filtration, having a retraction M_{α+1}→M_α and yielding a direct-summand decomposition.
references.reason: A split monomorphism/direct-summand structure is meaningful independently of transfinite dévissage.
references.matching_note: Match to splitting and direct summand constructions preserving map direction.

references.context: Transfinite algebra: continuity of increasing ordinal-indexed submodule filtration at a limit ordinal λ, requiring M_λ=⋃_{α<λ}M_α (the directed union) for each such λ.
references.reason: The limit-stage condition is reusable for filtrations of modules and differs from topological continuity.
references.matching_note: Avoid conflating continuity in real analysis and limit ordinal successor steps.

references.phrase: starting at zero and with union M
references.disposition: The zero-submodule and full-union conditions are explicitly part of this filtration's axioms.

references.phrase: finite free modules R^m and R^n
references.context: Module theory: finite-rank free R-modules R^m and R^n, finite direct sums of copies of R (including rank zero), distinct from arbitrary projectives.
references.reason: Finitely presented module descriptions use finite free modules explicitly.
references.matching_note: Compare to arbitrary free modules from free-resolution review without losing finiteness.

references.context: Module theory: a finite family of relations generating the kernel of a surjection R^n→M; the image of R^m→R^n equals the kernel of presentation map.
references.reason: Relations are independent algebraic data of the presentation, not implied by finite generation of M alone.
references.matching_note: Distinguish finitely generated relation submodule from polynomial relations for R-algebras.

references.disposition: Both generators and relations are finite; finite generation of M alone is insufficient over a non-Noetherian ring.
